submission.natural_language_explanation: L17/N4098+ fires where a text says or implements that ONE item is being taken out of a source: in prose the extraction verb itself (took, extracted, withdrew, snatched, plucked, seized, grabbed, removed, fetched, retrieved, pulled, picked, brought, got, Portuguese 'pega' - 'He walked to the shelf and took the red folder down' peaks at 6.4 on ' took' while the identical frame with left/touched/inspected/pushed stays at 0.76), and in code the call or operator that hands a single value across ('$this->_stmt->fetch(...)' 3.9, 'scanner.nextLine()' 3.7, 'getPropriedadeLimpar' 3.3 on the '::', '$_SESSION' 2.2 on ' $_', 'CACHE.get(id)' 1.9, '__getitem__', 'pop', 'RemoveFlag', 'load_command_class', 'Retrieves ...', and the ' =' of the item-at-a-time read loop 'while ($data = $this->_stmt->fetch(...))' 3.9). It is near zero when the same text acts on the whole collection instead of one item ('fetchAll'/foreach, array_map, .mapNotNull, .Items/.Rows/.Clear, list.entries: 0.01-0.35 - the regime where this neuron's negative pole fires at 1.7-8.3), and near zero on idiomatic or non-extraction uses of the same verbs ('It took two hours' 0.20, 'took the bus' 0.26, 'took a photo' 0.23, pushed/left/found/dropped 0.76); the unexplained leftovers are the weak (1.2-1.8) article/preposition tokens of Spanish and Portuguese code explanations (' la', ' el', ' de', ' uma').
